practices.headline: Add beans, lentils or chickpeas to one meal this week.
practices.how_to: For example, add chickpeas to a salad, lentils to a soup, or beans to a stew. Tinned ones are fine; rinse them first.

practices.headline: Taste your food before adding salt, and leave the salt shaker off the table at one meal today.
20 minutes of moderate cardio, such as a brisk walk, cycle or swim, 3 times this week.
practices.how_to: Use the talk test: you should be breathing harder but still able to talk in full sentences.

practices.headline: Try a short interval-style cardio session, alternating harder and easier periods.
practices.how_to: After a warm-up, try a few 20–30 second hard efforts with easy recovery between. If you're new to exercise or have a health condition, check with a professional first.

practices.headline: Leave your phone outside the bed, not in it or under the pillow.
practices.how_to: Put it on a bedside table or across the room, so your bed stays a place for sleep.

practices.headline: Spend 20 minutes in a nearby green space this week, such as a park, garden or woodland.
practices.how_to: Walk, sit on a bench or eat your lunch there. It counts towards a weekly total, so one visit or several short ones both work.

practices.headline: Include beans, lentils or chickpeas in at least 2 meals this week.
practices.how_to: A serving is about 100 g, roughly half a standard tin, drained.

practices.headline: Choose lower-salt versions of two foods you buy often this week.
practices.how_to: Compare labels on bread, cereals, sauces, soups, ready meals and processed meats, and pick the one with less salt. If a label shows only sodium, multiply it by 2.5 to get the salt content.

practices.headline: 20 minutes of moderate cardio on 5 days this week.
practices.how_to: That's 100 minutes a week, two-thirds of the way to the 150-minute recommendation. Keep using the talk test to check the effort.

practices.headline: Try a short interval-style cardio session, alternating harder and easier periods.
practices.how_to: After a warm-up, try a few 20–30 second hard efforts with easy recovery between. If you're new to exercise or have a health condition, check with a professional first.

practices.headline: List the groups you belong to, and pick one you'd like to be more involved in.
practices.how_to: Groups can be anything you feel part of: a club, team, class, faith community, volunteering group or group of friends.

practices.headline: 5 minutes of progressive muscle relaxation before bed: tense and release each muscle group in turn.
practices.how_to: Lying in bed, work from your feet up to your face. Tense each muscle group firmly (never to the point of pain) for a few seconds, then let go and notice the release. Moving through your feet, legs, stomach, hands, arms, shoulders and face takes about 5 minutes.

practices.headline: Practise slow, conscious breathing for a few minutes, keeping your out-breath longer than your in-breath.
practices.how_to: Try cyclic sighing for about 5 minutes: breathe in through your nose, add a second short inhale to fill your lungs, then breathe out slowly through your mouth.

practices.headline: Give a hug to someone close to you today, if they welcome it.
practices.how_to: Ask first if you're not sure.

hygiene_priority.text: Cut bedroom noise: close windows on the noisy side, move away from noise sources, or try foam earplugs.
